why: Items 5 and 7 both mix fighting off damage with quietly watching and fixing the mark, and the gate between defence and repair is the hardest to hold in these packets.

why.T3-047: The item is a false-attack quarrel between two subs closed by apology, thanks and good wishes, which is T3-047; T3-040 fails because no damage was done to apologise for.
why.T3-011: Pixels and members are also sent to help r/Tokyo's work with nothing asked, T3-011's gate, distinct from the making-up.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-047 reaches the apology and thanks that close the quarrel but not the sending of pixels and members to help r/Tokyo.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0055039 and C1129041 send help to r/Tokyo with nothing asked, satisfying T3-011.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-011; dropping it loses the mutual-help side of the exchange.

why.T3-041: The recurring act is adding letters and another piece beside the finished mark, T3-041's gate; the design talk rides on that enlargement.
why.T3-004: Colours, spacing and the smiley are worked out and corrected against the plan, T3-004's gate, in concepts of their own.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-041's gate covers the added letters and the proposed further expansion but not the choice of blue, purple and letter spacing.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1524200 and C0290035 argue the mark's colours, spacing and smiley, satisfying T3-004.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-004; dropping it loses the look of the enlarged mark.

why.T3-054: After placement ended the room rebuilds its flag on r/placetwo, an alternative canvas, T3-054's gate; it is not a move after a loss on the same canvas (T3-022) or a new sub (T3-111).

why.T3-023: The moderators restyled the sub for April Fools by swapping the sidebar picture, and members play inside it, noticing, laughing and sharing the picture; T3-001 fails because the joke is the sub's changed look, not a member's fake post.

why.T3-005: The leading act is fighting off vandals and erasure of the flag, T3-005's gate; watching and repair (T3-021), upkeep over expansion (T3-042) and first-build reports (T3-038) also meet their floors and are listed.

why.T3-033: The most concepts of their own offer the room ideas for what to make (the swarm pattern, a bug faction, the C53 logo, the red back), T3-033's gate; template/direction (T3-070), defence (T3-005) and building (T3-038) also meet their floors and are listed.

why.T3-073: The bulk of the concepts report what happened to the logo (still standing, gone, disappearing, altered wording), T3-073's gate.
why.T3-087: Other concepts work out who changed it (a grey brick, a bot user, calling out a failed grief), T3-087's gate, distinct from the reporting.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-073's gate tells what happened to the work but does not reach the naming of who altered it.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C1243693, C1394668 and C0765627 trace and name the source of the damage, satisfying T3-087.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-087; dropping it loses the attribution of the damage.

why.T3-073: The concepts reconstruct what happened to the grid (the alien overwritten, the hive takeover, the history), T3-073's gate; they tell the work's past rather than argue a detail's meaning (T3-018) or trace a live attacker (T3-087).

why.T3-009: The many celebration concepts (we did it, unscathed, only distro to survive) are T3-009's gate.
why.T3-073: Concepts also recount what happened to the logo and to neighbours (fought off trey, buffered Estonia, fixed neighbours' pixels), T3-073's gate, distinct from the celebrating.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-009's gate marks the work as achieved but does not reach the recounting of what happened to it and to neighbours.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0883777, C0160137, C0605589 and C1357264 tell what happened to the work, satisfying T3-073.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-073; dropping it loses the retelling that runs through the item.

why.T3-016: The one surviving concept is a submission titled about r/place with no body left, so the least-wrong placement is a post about what the canvas is rather than any action on a mark.
Every concept asks or answers what r/place is, the announcement, the one-pixel/five-minute rules and how people form and protect art, T3-016's gate; it is not a guide to the room's own work (T3-070).

why.T3-001: Members reply inside an April Fools prank in their own sub, folding the repeated-link error into the fake and keeping the tease going, which is T3-001's reply-inside-a-fake; T3-031 fails because it is tied to the April Fools prank.

why.T3-017: The bulk of the item is ordinary PC talk (game recommendations, build advice, troubleshooting, giveaways) carried on alongside the event, T3-017's gate.
why.T3-063: A recurring set of concepts has the sub's rules applied to event posts, removals with 'Breach of Rule' notices, T3-063's gate, distinct from ordinary talk.

multiplacement_log.why_not_one: T3-017's gate covers the ordinary talk going on but does not reach the moderators removing event posts under the standing rules.
multiplacement_log.why_this_one: C0856735, C0545283, C1113619 and C1357730 apply the sub's rules to event posts, satisfying T3-063.
multiplacement_log.dispensable: T3-063; dropping it loses the removals running under the ordinary rules.

why.T3-023: The moderators change the sub itself for April Fools (missing voting arrows, imposed Stonoga styling, a quotation game, a disguised Rickroll) and members play inside and dispute it, T3-023's gate; T3-032 fails because the objections are few.
